_meta.description: Parametric cardinal-temperature / humidity niche curves for the six seed species. Suitability is a predicted niche-fit score, not a detection or an occurrence probability.
sources: Pitt & Hocking, Fungi and Food Spoilage (3rd ed., 2009) - cardinal temperatures and water-activity/RH minima for Aspergillus and Eurotium.
Flannigan & Miller (2011), Microbial growth in indoor environments; Grant et al. (1989) - Aspergillus versicolor T/RH growth isopleths.
Andersen, Nielsen & Jarvis (2002), Stachybotrys chartarum microcolony growth; Flannigan & Miller - high-RH requirement.
Andrews & Pitt (1987), xerophilic Eurotium spp. water relations; Samson, Hoekstra & Frisvad (2004).
Ramos et al. (1998) and Pitt & Hocking (2009) - Aspergillus ochraceus group ecophysiology.
Data INRAE Fusarium ecophysiology records - Fusarium cardinal temperatures and high-aw requirement.
Values are rounded literature midpoints and are meant for ranking, not regulatory or clinical decisions.
_meta.lux_note: lux_pref is an optional triangular modifier. Where sources are light-agnostic the curve spans normal indoor light so it barely changes the ranking.

species.name: Aspergillus versicolor
species.note: Common indoor mould; grows from ~4 C, optimum near 25 C, needs RH above ~65 %.

species.name: Stachybotrys chartarum
species.note: Requires sustained very-wet conditions (RH >= 90 %); low-light competitor.

species.name: Eurotium herbariorum
species.note: Xerophilic; can grow at lower RH than the other seed species.

species.name: Aspergillus niger
species.note: Warm-adapted; broad temperature range, high RH optimum.

species.name: Aspergillus ochraceus group
species.note: Ochratoxin-producing group; warm and humid preference.

species.name: Fusarium spp.
species.note: High water-activity requirement; curve informed by Data INRAE ecophysiology records.
